results.evidence: WTA's Upper South Fork Skokomish hike and its Six Ridge hike both describe the Six Ridge route starting at the Upper Skokomish trailhead and climbing to Sundown Pass (7.2 mi) and Sundown Lake, matching this row's waypoints, road and approach. Day mileages/gains were left as stored (not re-derived) per the no-arithmetic rule.

results.fact: Where the Mount Olson Way leaves Six Ridge / high camp
results.evidence: Trip reports place the unsigned 'Mt. Olson Way Trail' sign on the ridge proper beyond Six Ridge Pass, in the stretch with the old McGravey Lakes camp and Belview camp; McGravey Lakes sits about 1.5 mi east of Sundown Pass by map (~47.545,-123.487, ~4,000 ft), so the stored 8.7 mi (1.5 mi past the pass) is probably too short, and the trailhead note's '~11 miles' is the full length of the Six Ridge crest to the North Fork (WTA), not the distance to the Olson spur. No two sources give a mileage for the junction, so no patch; the 8.7 distMi does not break waypoint order so it was not nulled.

results.correct_value: No parking pass or NP entrance fee at the Upper South Fork Skokomish trailhead; only the wilderness camping permit applies for overnights.
results.evidence: WTA's Upper South Fork Skokomish page lists 'Parking pass/entry fee: None'. The Forest Service Skokomish Upper/Lower South Fork Trailhead page (same coordinates as this route's trailhead pin, 47.48632,-123.45775) states no fees are required. The FS Lower South Fork trail page requires a recreation pass only at the separate Lower trailhead on FR 2353. There is no NPS entrance station on this approach, so the NP entrance-fee text did not apply.

results.evidence: Explore Hood Canal gives Lake Sundown's elevation as 3,810 ft; the USGS-name-derived topozone entry (Mount Hoquiam quad) gives ~3,825 ft at 47.5355,-123.5103 (same spot as the waypoint). WTA notes the trail descends ~400 ft from the 4,125 ft pass, consistent with the lake sitting below the pass, not at 4,030 ft. The waypoint's 3810 stands; the approach variant's 4,030 was the outlier.

results.evidence: There are two South Fork Skokomish crossings: Explore Hood Canal describes a first crossing near 1.3 mi (on a fallen cedar) and a second later, both safe only in late-summer/early-fall low water, and WTA names the unbridged ford at 2.4 mi the 'second Skokomish crossing'. The waypoint marks only the unbridged one, which does not deny the first; 'two fords' is consistent.

Both fields agree: the Bear Gulch Fire closure covers the eastern Six Ridge Trail (east edge of Belview Camp down to the North Fork), which WTA confirms, while the South Fork Skokomish/Sundown Pass approach used here stays open. It is also a bivy-only field, which is handled elsewhere.

results.fact: Current status of the Upper South Fork Skokomish trail after the Bear Gulch Fire
results.evidence: The Forest Service trailhead page still carries an 'August 1, 2025: Upper South Fork Skokomish River Trail currently closed due to Bear Gulch Fire' alert, while access.closures says the fire does not affect this approach. The alert may be stale (a 2026 news item mentions only a short Aug 12-13, 2026 access closure), and no second source settles the current status, so no change.
